subject: Physics
source: IISER IAT 2025, final answer key (English), iiseradmission.in
_transcription: Pages p48-p61 of the 2025 render, one question per page (p48 = Q1 under the 'Physics' heading ... p61 = Q14). Each page prints 'N. Question N' and the subject's own page footer 1-14; numbers run 1-14 unbroken with no continuation or blank pages. Only 14 questions are printed: IISER dropped one Physics question from its final key, so there is no 15th row. The 'Question N' header line is dropped from the stems. Options kept in printed order. Q1's options are graphs (optionFigures); Q2, Q3, Q8, Q9, Q12 and Q13 carry a stem figure.

rows.text: Consider an elastic collision between two particles \(A\) and \(B\) of same mass, moving in the same direction. Particle \(A\) is moving at speed \(v_A\) and particle \(B\) is moving at speed \(v_B\). In the figures shown, the solid lines represent the motion before the collision and the dotted lines represent the motion after the collision. Which of the following describes the motion of these two particles most accurately?
options: x-t graph: solid A (steeper, from the origin) meets solid B (shallower, starting above the origin); after the meeting the steeper dotted line is B and the shallower dotted line is A. v-t graph: solid A above solid B before the collision; dotted B above dotted A after it

x-t graph: solid A (steeper, from the origin) meets solid B (shallower, starting above the origin); after the meeting the steeper dotted line is B and the shallower dotted line is A. v-t graph: solid A above solid B before the collision; dotted A above dotted B after it

x-t graph: solid A (steeper, from the origin) meets solid B (shallower, starting above the origin); after the meeting the steeper dotted line is B and the shallower dotted line is A. v-t graph: solid B above solid A before the collision; dotted A above dotted B after it

x-t graph: solid A (steeper, from the origin) meets solid B (shallower, starting above the origin); after the meeting the steeper dotted line is B and the shallower dotted line is A. v-t graph: solid B above solid A before the collision; dotted B above dotted A after it

rows.text: A block of mass \(M\) lies at rest connected to a massless spring of spring constant \(k\) on a frictionless surface. A bullet of mass \(m\) hits the block horizontally with speed \(v\) as shown in the figure and is completely stuck to the block. What is the maximum compression in the spring resulting from this impact (assuming that at this point the spring is still not fully compressed)?

figure.note: Wall on the left; a spring labelled k joins the wall to a block labelled M on a horizontal floor; a bullet labelled m approaches the block from the right, with an arrow labelled v pointing left towards the block.

rows.subtopic: Potential Energy and Conservation of Mechanical Energy
rows.text: A cart of mass \(M\) is released from \(A\), the highest point of a frictionless track, as shown in the figure. The cart travels along the track and enters the semicircular arc \(DBC\) of radius \(R\). The heights of the points \(A\) and \(B\) are \(h_1\) and \(h_2\) from the ground, respectively. Which of the following quantities does not play any role in ensuring that the cart does not leave the track?

figure.note: A cart at point A at the top of a curved frictionless track; a dotted vertical arrow labelled h1 from A down to the dashed ground line. The track runs down and into a vertical circular loop: B at the top, C on the left, D on the right. Inside the loop a dotted vertical arrow labelled h2 rises from the centre to B, and a dotted horizontal arrow labelled 2R runs between C and D. Small arrows show the direction of travel down the slope and round the loop; the track exits to the right along the ground.

rows.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
rows.subtopic: Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fixed Axis
rows.text: A circular disk of mass \(M\) and radius \(R\) is rotating clockwise with a uniform angular velocity \(\omega\) about an axis passing through the centre, normal to the disk. At time \(t = 0\), a torque \(T\) is applied along the same axis to oppose the rotation of the disk. What is the angular displacement \(\theta\) (measured from \(t = 0\) in the clockwise direction) that the disk attains before it starts rotating counterclockwise?

A metallic cube initially kept at a temperature \(T\) is emitting black body radiation with a power \(P\) (energy emitted per unit time). If \(T\) is increased by \(1\%\), the power being radiated increases by \(4.5\%\). What is the approximate percentage increase in the volume of the cube in this process?

rows.subtopic: Superposition of Waves and Standing Waves
rows.text: Consider two pipes \(A\) and \(B\) of identical length. \(A\) has one end closed and one end open. \(B\) has both ends open. Each tube is immersed in a closed chamber of ideal gas having volume \(V\). The chamber containing tube \(A\) is at temperature \(T_A\) and the chamber containing tube \(B\) is at temperature \(T_B\). The sound frequencies corresponding to the \(n_A\)-th harmonic in tube \(A\) and the \(n_B\)-th harmonic in tube \(B\) are the same. What is the relation between the temperatures \(T_A\) and \(T_B\)?

rows.subtopic: Superposition of Waves and Standing Waves
rows.text: Consider two waves, which are given by \(y_1(x, t) = A\sin(kx - \omega t)\) and \(y_2(x, t) = \sqrt{3}A\cos(kx - \omega t)\), where \(k\) is the wave number and \(\omega\) is the angular frequency. The amplitude of the resultant waveform obtained by the superposition of the two waves is \(A_s\) and its phase difference with \(y_1\) is \(\phi_s\). What are \(A_s\) and \(\phi_s\)?

A particle of charge \(q = 1e\) and mass \(m\) with kinetic energy \(K\) enters an electric field set up by two parallel plates of length \(l\) as illustrated in the figure. The potential difference between the two plates is 1 V and their separation is \(d\). What is the minimum value of \(K\) (in eV) for which the particle will not hit either of the plates?
[\(e\) is the charge of the electron.]

figure.note: Two horizontal parallel plates: the top plate labelled 1 V, the bottom plate 0 V, separation d (double arrow on the right), length l (double arrow below). An arrow labelled E points down between the plates. A particle labelled q, m enters from the left moving horizontally (arrow to the right), at a distance d/2 below the top plate (marked with a vertical arrow labelled d/2).

rows.text: What is the potential difference between the points \(P\) and \(Q\) in the circuit shown below, once the capacitors are fully charged?

figure.note: A diamond of four capacitors with P at the top corner and Q at the bottom corner. Upper-left arm (left corner to P): 4 \u03bcF; upper-right arm (P to right corner): 2 \u03bcF; lower-left arm (left corner to Q): 2 \u03bcF; lower-right arm (Q to right corner): 4 \u03bcF. The left and right corners are wired to a 12V battery below the diamond.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Force and Motion in a Magnetic Field
rows.text: A particle of mass \(m\) and charge \(q\) moving with a velocity \(\vec{v} = v_0(\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k})\) is placed in a uniform magnetic field \(\vec{B} = B_0(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k})\). It executes a helical trajectory of radius \(r\) and pitch \(p\). Which of the following options is correct?

A charged particle is moving in a circular orbit with radius \(r\) and orbital angular frequency \(\omega\) in the presence of a magnetic field. The orbit is enclosed within a larger circular metallic frame. The frame is concentric and coplanar with the orbit. The radius of the frame is now gradually decreased. Assuming that the particle remains within the frame at all times, what changes to the trajectory of the particle will occur as the frame is being shrunk?
options: The radius of the orbit will gradually decrease and the frequency will gradually increase.
The radius of the orbit will gradually increase and the frequency will gradually decrease.
The radius of the orbit will remain the same but the frequency will gradually increase.
Both the radius of the orbit and the frequency will remain unchanged.

rows.text: Consider an equilateral prism of refractive index 1.5 and a parallelepiped block of refractive index 2.0 arranged as shown in the figure such that their adjacent faces are parallel. A light ray enters the prism from air at an angle of incidence such that the ray travels through the prism parallel to its base. What is the angle of emergence \(\theta\)?

figure.note: An equilateral prism labelled n = 1.5 (surrounding air labelled n = 1.0) beside a parallelepiped block labelled n = 2.0, the prism's right face parallel to the block's left face with an air gap between. A ray enters the prism's left face from the lower left, travels horizontally (parallel to the base) through the prism, crosses the gap into the block and leaves its right face; dashed normals are drawn at the block's faces, and the emergent ray makes the angle labelled theta at the block's right face.

rows.text: A source produces a light beam of intensity \(I_0\) polarized along the \(x\)-direction. The beam is sent along the \(z\)-direction. It enters a polaroid \(P1\) with its polaroid axis aligned along the \(y\)-direction so that no light exits the polaroid. When another polaroid \(P2\) is placed in between the source and \(P1\), the intensity measured after \(P1\) is \(3I_0/16\). Which among the following is a possible value of \(\theta\), the angle of the polaroid axis measured from the \(x\)-axis?

figure.note: Axes at the left: x up, z to the right, y slanting down-right. A double arrow along x labelled 'Polarisation of incident light' and the beam labelled I0 travel along z through polaroid P2, whose axis (dotted arrow) is at an angle marked 'theta?' from the x direction, then through polaroid P1, whose axis is drawn along y (marked with a right-angle sign against the x arrow). The beam leaving P1 is labelled 3I0/16.

rows.subtopic: Bohr Model of the Hydrogen Atom
rows.text: An electron in the ground state (with energy \(E_1\)) of a hydrogen atom, absorbs a photon of energy \(E_a\), and gets excited to a higher energy level of principal quantum number \(n\). What is the value of \(n\)?
